svg.title: TOPAK E5 — Two bounds below the intent boundary: revocation bounded in effects, with no premise about time, and duration bounded by the plane's ticks, under a declared premise
svg.desc: A plane that is cut off cannot tell "not revoked" from "revoked, and not yet heard". ADR-0063 makes it stop on something of its own: the intent boundary reads the plane's record and answers with watermarks, and a plane may have fewer than K_up effects outstanding, a count with no clock in it. ADR-0064 adds the bound a count cannot give, on duration: the plane's clock is its ticks, numbered from the charter and each signed by a certificate of replicas on their own clocks, with every interval a count of ticks from a named tick. The second bound has a premise about time and the first has none, and that is why they are two records (ADR-0064 Findings, 2). Both are Proposed, both are an overlay and not the archetype, and nothing here is built.
svg.text: TOPAK · E5

own clocks, with every interval a count of ticks from a named tick. The second bound has a premise about time and the first has none, and that is why they are two records (ADR-0064 Findings, 2). Both are Proposed, both are an overlay and not the archetype, and nothing here is built.

Lean arithmetic of ADR-0064 §2's two rules

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian decided ⟨2⟩ (the TTL as the safety parameter, later overtaken), ⟨12⟩ (revocation is bounded in effects, and that is the safety property), ⟨13⟩ (a clock held by a quorum as the second bound, for duration), ⟨18⟩ (a governor's own clock as a watchdog only), answered ⟨Q11⟩, ⟨Q12⟩ and ⟨Q13⟩, and on 2026.11.10 decided that overdue is by the governor's own clock. Every other choice is the drafter's. R1 took the modules' findings the same day. Checked

is TLC's rows at small constants; proved is TLAPS obligations under each module's assumptions; neither word is used of running code, and there is none. One author, one day, and §4's argument as corrected has been read by its author only (ADR-0063 §8).

text.tspan: The record goes up, the watermark comes down, and what no watermark covers stays under
Proposed · C1 · nothing here is built
Above: the intent boundary, the commanded plane's mechanism (ADR-0060)
The intent boundary's mechanism: the plane's Observer ⟨12⟩

svg.text: This is R3-observer-live's shape (ToO §5.4), pointed upward (§1).
It archives a segment of the plane's record and runs its checks, then orders a watermark. What those checks are is open (Open obligations).
The watermark is the mechanism's act. No person signs it ⟨Q12⟩: the plane's tempo would be that person's attention (Options).
Its reading is a trust root for the watermark (T-0068-5): a watermark for a record nobody checked releases a charge nobody read (Consequences).
Stops a plane by a fence or a revocation, and not by withholding attention ⟨Q12⟩.
The intent boundary orders it, and every watermark ordered after it carries the moved fence (§2, §4).
Charges what is outstanding: a lease's whole count when the lease is granted, and an ordered entry when it is admitted.

text.tspan: A charge is released when a watermark covers it.

svg.text: Grants no lease, and admits no ordered entry, that would take the charge to K_up. The charter gains kUp.
A plane is a havoc issuer (ADR-0059 §4). Under capture its charge means nothing, and each governor's account below does (Outstanding's header).
Cells charged by leases' counts and ordered entries that no watermark covers yet.
Strict: the charge, with this grant, stays under K_up, so the capacity is K_up − 1. "At most K_up" lets one more through (M_ATMOST).

text.tspan: Each vehicle: a governor and a stack (ADR-0062 §1)
Governor g1: its own account, kept for itself ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: Accepts a lease, or carries out an ordered entry, only if its own leases and ordered entries that no watermark covers, with this one, stay under K_up.
Checks each watermark's certificate against the chain. It does not take its plane's word for what has been read (M_TRUSTMARK).
Its own leases' counts and its ordered entries, uncovered: under K_up, strictly.
Under a captured plane, each honest vehicle produces fewer than K_up effects after a revocation (§4).
Writes each entry it permits or refuses to a chain, and at the lease's end seals it; the plane orders the seal (ADR-0062 §6).
Its own leases' counts and its ordered entries, uncovered: under K_up, strictly.
The link (T-0068-11, delegated). Loss only subtracts
: cut, no watermark arrives and the plane stops
granting before K_up (§5).
its log, with each lease's sealed record, as it is made, while
the link holds (§1)
a watermark, with a commit certificate (§2; ADR-0059
a fence or a revocation: pushed, and pulled in every watermark
a lease: its whole count charged at the grant

text.tspan: A watermark carries three things, and a certificate (§2)
The plane index it has read through.
The digests of the lease records sealed in that segment.

svg.text: The fences of every plane above, so the fence is pulled as well as pushed (ADR-0059 §6).
It comes down with a commit certificate (ADR-0059 §5). A captured plane cannot forge one, nor a vehicle's seal (Outstanding's header).
It covers one segment and is not cumulative (§4).
ADR-0039 couples a Thinker's admits to its Observer's watermark: seq(t) − mark(o, r) < K, a count and not a time, strict because ≤ K
admits a K+1 backlog, which Coupling.tla found.
ADR-0063 points that shape upward: the intent boundary reads the plane, and what it has not read stays under K_up.
Reported upstream under ADR-0058 §6 ⟨Q11⟩: liveness coupled to admission between planes, and a record read as it is made. If the archetype
takes them, ADR-0039, ADR-0031 and ADR-0005 owe entries (§7).
With the link above cut, no watermark arrives, the charge only grows, and the plane stops granting before K_up. Vehicles spend the leases
they hold, and then hold.
The first revision's pushed fence failed open: no news meant carry on until T_intent.
A jammed plane stops after K_up effects (Consequences). A small K_up stops it sooner; a large one lets more through under a revoked intent.
What the intent boundary has read is archived above. A captured plane's log is not evidence, and that now holds of the unread tail only, fewer
than K_up effects.

text.tspan: The seal, and a vehicle alone (ADR-0062 §5, §6)

svg.text: Under a lease the governor writes each entry it permits or refuses to a chain on the vehicle, hash-linked and signed. At the lease's end it seals
the chain, and the plane orders the seal as one entry and runs the mechanism checks there.
Nothing a governor permitted is void: the effect has happened. A check that fails at the seal, or above, is a finding, and can only subtract. A

text.tspan: captured vehicle's chain is not evidence.

svg.text: A vehicle that stops hearing its plane is alone and loses its lease at once: it permits no actuation, keeps listening, and may send a beacon
within its count, which is an effect ⟨R1⟩.
the plane (P, the replicas)
the mechanism: the intent boundary's, and each governor's
a fence or a revocation: only removes authority
a charge cell: outstanding, not yet covered
K_up: never reached

text.tspan: What is charged, the strict rule, and each governor's own account (ADR-0063 §3, as revised ⟨R1⟩)
Proposed · C1: a condition on every grant an autonomous plane makes
What is charged, and what releases it

svg.text: A lease's whole count, when the lease is granted; an ordered entry, when it is admitted.

text.tspan: A charge is released when a watermark covers it.

svg.text: What is charged is an effect: a local entry and an ordered one, as ADR-0042 §2 counts effects for an Observer.
Not charged: a report to a peer topic (ADR-0065); a tick, which is not an effect.

text.tspan: The plane grants no lease, and admits no
entry, that would take the outstanding charge to

svg.text: "At most K_up" lets one more through, which ADR-0039's model found of K (M_ATMOST).
The capacity is K_up − 1, and a kUp of one grants nothing: NeverGranted holds at KUp = 1 (row w-k1-nogrant;
Outstanding finding 4).

text.tspan: or more can never be granted.
Each governor keeps the same account for itself ⟨R1⟩

svg.text: It accepts a lease, or carries out an ordered entry, only if the counts of its own leases and ordered entries that no
watermark covers, with this one, stay under K_up.
M_ORDEREDFREE: a rule that named only leases, as §3 first read, lets a captured plane admit ordered entries without
limit (Outstanding finding 1).
M_TRUSTMARK: a governor that takes its plane's word for what has been read. A plane is a havoc issuer (ADR-0059
§4), so a governor checks each watermark's certificate against the chain.

text.tspan: Why at the grant, and where the floor would carry it

svg.text: A governor's permits are not ordered (ADR-0062 §2), so the charge is taken at the grant (Options: "count at each
permit" is not available).
FD10-outstanding-bound (ADR-0067 §3, R1) would forbid both: at the plane, a grant or ordered admit that takes the
charge to K_up; at a governor, a lease or ordered entry that takes its own there. Not written.
K_up is a placeholder: at least 2 and above any lease's count, and its relation to an intent's budget is open.

text.tspan: What that bounds, with no premise about time, and the argument as revised (ADR-0063 §4, §6; Context)
Proposed · §4's argument read by its author only
Effects after a revocation are bounded

svg.text: After the intent boundary orders a revocation or a fence, the vehicles of an honest plane produce fewer than K_up further effects. Under a captured plane, each honest vehicle produces fewer than
K_up. A vehicle revoked by its own plane produces at most what is left of its lease's count
A narrower intent or a tightened bundle cannot reach a plane that is cut off. Superseded rules govern fewer than K_up effects there
An intent never grants more leases than its budget. A lease never permits more entries than its count. An entry never runs past its extent (ADR-0062 §4)
"Clocks buy liveness, never safety." The bound in §4 reads no clock. C3 does not apply, and this is the point of the record: the proposal's first revision reversed the clause (Status note; Context).

The lattice analysis proposes that no safety theorem have a timing premise among its ancestors, so that the clause is computed and not only stated. §4's properties meet that: no variable or guard in Outstanding is a time (§8).
What a clock can still extend is one entry in progress, by the residual ADR-0064 §5 states (band 4).

text.tspan: The Context's precedents: the corpus has met a clock problem four times and has not once answered with a better clock

svg.text: ADR-0034's nonce is a hash of epoch and log index, "so freshness comes from the log and not a clock" (ToO §2.6). ADR-0050's sign-on is fresh "because of what it
names" (ToO §7.10)

text.tspan: Took an interval's origin from the log

svg.text: ADR-0039's bound on unread effects is "a count, not a time" (ToO §5.4)

text.tspan: Counted the mechanism's own acts, which have no drift

svg.text: ADR-0039 coupled liveness to admission, so that a dead Observer stops its Thinker
R8, the break-glass TTL, was withdrawn because it needed trusted time, and ADR-0045 refused a time source (ToO §10)

text.tspan: A log orders and does not measure (Context)

svg.text: ADR-0032: "Causality orders events and bounds no interval."
A fence is a message, and a plane that is cut off cannot tell "not revoked" from "revoked, and not yet heard". So it has to stop on something of its own. A count of its own acts is exact.
§4's argument for the first row, as revised ⟨R1⟩, step by step (Outstanding findings 2 and 3)

text.tspan: ① Watermarks after the revocation carry the fence
Every watermark ordered after the revocation carries the moved

svg.text: fence, since every watermark carries the fences of every plane above

text.tspan: ② The stop on hearing one carries the bound

svg.text: A plane or a governor that hears one stops. A later watermark
releases a charge whose lease may have produced effects after the
revocation.
A hearer that released it and went on granting would break the bound:
M_NOSTOP (finding 3).

text.tspan: ③ What was covered before is sealed
Every lease covered by a watermark ordered before the revocation

svg.text: is sealed and produces nothing more: SealedIsSpent (
M_EARLYRELEASE breaks it).

text.tspan: ④ A watermark is not cumulative

svg.text: It covers one segment. So what stays charged is what no watermark
ordered before the revocation covers, and not only what the last one left
(finding 2).

text.tspan: ⑤ So every later effect is already charged
Every effect after the revocation is charged to a lease or an entry

svg.text: that no pre-revocation watermark covers, and those charges together
stay under K_up (§3's strict rule).

text.tspan: ⑥ Delay only lowers what is released

svg.text: An adversary can deliver such a watermark late or not at all, which
only lowers what is released.
No clock is read at any step (§6).

text.tspan: An autonomous plane's clock is its ticks: numbered from the charter, signed by a certificate on its replicas' own clocks (ADR-0064 §1–§6)
Proposed · no confirmation criterion · nothing here is built

svg.text: Ticks numbered from the charter, and the stall the first draft would have hidden (§1; Findings 1)
A stall: an adversary lets no tick through, for a week, say, and then lets one through

text.tspan: §1: tick τ says τ periods of
have passed since the charter was

svg.text: applied. The numbers need not be consecutive. Each replica keeps one
reading of its own monotonic clock, taken at the charter.
The first draft: each period measured from the tick before. Rejected
(Findings 1; Options); M_RELATIVETICK breaks NoGrantPastExpiry.

Real time, in periods of T_tick from the charter's application (tick zero). Numbered from the charter, the first tick after the stall carries it (11). From the tick before, the count moves by one (5), and the
stall is hidden. Schematic positions.
The charter gains tick, the period. The first intent counts from tick zero
§2: two rules on a replica's vote, and which carries what ⟨R1⟩

text.tspan: Rule 1: never sign a tick ahead of its own clock
A replica signs tick τ only when its own elapsed time has reached τ periods.

svg.text: It carries availability, ADR-0032's liveness side: it stops a captured or fast quorum burning a plane's
intervals.
It carries no property in PlaneClock: a tick ahead of real time moves an expiry and an extent nearer,
which only subtracts (the module's finding on §2).

text.tspan: Rule 2: never sign a grant behind its own clock
A replica signs no lease and no
admit while, by its own clock read with the early margin
(ADR-0031 E1), the next tick is due.

svg.text: It carries §4's bound: NoGrantPastExpiry rests on it.
No time crosses a boundary: a replica reads its own clock and signs or does not. No timestamp is
exchanged and no external time is read, so ADR-0032 §3 holds as written.
The arithmetic of the two rules is to be transcribed and proved, as mechanism/lean/Topak/Clock.lean does for the subtracting interval (§8). Not met.
How far the rules fit PBFT's validity check (ADR-0061 §2) is open, once PBFT is read.

text.tspan: §3: every interval is a number of ticks from a named tick ⟨Q13⟩

svg.text: An intent's expiry, a lease's ttl, a charter's expiry, an entry's duration and a release act's freshness are tick numbers. Each end is a comparison in the log:
the same on every replica, and checkable again at apply, which a per-replica clock is not (ToO §15 found that of T_obs).
An intent names a tick the plane has handed up, and its expiry counts from that tick.
A lease's ttl counts from the tick at which the plane ordered the grant, and ends no later than its intent's expiry.
The first intent counts from the charter's application, tick zero ⟨Q13⟩. It is granted by the promotion, before the plane has ticked.
Anything withheld for a day arrives a day old. That is the answer to the NATO reading's F1: an interval that starts at receipt can be started late by whoever holds
the message (M_RECEIPT).
Premise: captured and slow replicas together are fewer than a certificate. At seven replicas that is at most four (ADR-0061 §1). A replica is slow when its clock
lags by more than its margin.
Then every certificate includes a replica that is neither captured nor slow. It signed only because, by a sound clock, the latest tick was current. So at every
grant the tick count is less than one period behind real time, and no grant is made under an intent more than one tick period past its expiry. A lease ends no
later than its intent, so effects are bounded too, up to §5's residual.
A fast clock only subtracts: it refuses grants early, and draws on the silence a plane tolerates.
A declared bound, not a safety theorem. With the premise false the bound fails (M_TOOSLOW) ⟨R1⟩, and ADR-0063's bound still holds.
a certificate: 5 of 7 (ADR-0061 §1)
captured or slow: at most 4
sound

text.tspan: §5: a governor's own clock decides one thing: that the next tick is overdue ⟨18⟩

svg.text: A governor counts an entry's duration in ticks, and checks each tick number against its own elapsed time. When the next tick is overdue, the vehicle is
alone and the lease ends (ADR-0062 §5).
Overdue is by the governor's own clock ⟨R1⟩, on the custodian's decision of 2026.11.10: the next tick is overdue when that clock reaches the tick's due time.
Under a captured plane the ticks are the captor's, and the duration bound for an honest vehicle rests on that governor's own clock, which treats a lagging tick as
overdue.
A slow governor clock finds a tick overdue late, and can stretch the entry in progress, only when the plane's ticks have also stopped reaching it. A bound
on a declared value, plus drift: the shape of ADR-0045's finding 2.
Reachable: NeverStretched is violated with a slow governor (w-stretched-slow), and holds with a sound or fast one.
Nothing else reaches it: NoStretchUnlessSlow, proved.

text.tspan: §6's table, whole: the trades are declared

svg.text: A short loss of signal ends a lease
A longer stretch for an entry in progress when the plane is gone
A plane stopped at K_up gives up waiting for the link sooner
An idle plane may act on an older intent

T_tick has to be long against a round of the plane over its radios, or ticks fall behind and leases end with no adversary present (§6; A-0068-10). Both values are placeholders, and a measurement of a round is owed (Open obligations).
ADR-0032 §2's table (ratified, B5), and the row ADR-0064 §7 says it would owe if the archetype took the overlay
Subtracts authority
a local monotonic clock, read with an asymmetric margin
lease expiry, passive e-stop, vote timeout
Adds or preserves authority
trusted time: a signed, attested time source outside the principal
break-glass TTL, Persona expiry, re-attestation intervals
Owed, not written (ADR-0064 §7)
an interval read by a quorum of local clocks, beside "local clock" and "trusted time"
an intent's expiry and a lease's ttl in ticks, at a plane that has them

text.tspan: The two bounds fail differently, and that is why they are two records (ADR-0064 Findings, 2)
ADR-0064: duration, bounded by the plane's ticks

svg.text: None about time. No variable or guard in Outstanding is a time (§8)
Captured and slow replicas together are fewer than a certificate (§4), and each sound clock's margin covers its drift (A-0068-2). The module's named ASSUME ClockPremise
Effects after a revocation or a fence: fewer than K_up from an honest plane, or from each honest vehicle under a captured one. Stale rules, and exposure (§4's table)
Duration: no grant under an intent more than one tick period past its expiry (§4). A lease ends no later than its intent, so effects too, up to §5's residual
The mechanism's own acts: a count, exact, with no drift (Context)
Ticks: numbered entries in the log, from the charter, each signed by a certificate (§1)
Each honest governor's own account, and the intent boundary's reading, a trust root for the watermark (T-0068-5)
A plane's clocks, taken together: a trust root for the duration bound only (T-0068-3). The governor's clock: a residual in the slow direction (T-0068-2)

text.tspan: When it fails, or under capture

svg.text: No premise to fail. Under a captured plane, each honest governor still bounds its own vehicle (HavocPlaneBoundedInEffects). A cut link fails closed (§5)

With the premise false the bound fails (M_TOOSLOW): NoGrantPastExpiry is void and EffectsAfterRevocationBounded is not (A-0068-2; TM14). Under a captured plane the ticks are the captor's, and the duration bound is the
honest governor's own clock
A plane that idles and then acts on an old intent is inside it. ADR-0064 is for that (Consequences)
A slow governor clock stretches the entry in progress, only when the ticks have also stopped reaching it (§5)
Its first clause stands: the bound reads no clock (§6). C3 does not apply
Kept, with a residual (Status note). A declared bound and not a safety theorem in the lattice analysis's sense (§4)
Outstanding: EffectsAfterRevocationBounded, HavocPlaneBoundedInEffects, SealedIsSpent, CountExact. 1,871 obligations proved, with no hypothesis about time; checked in 40 rows at KUp 2 and 3
PlaneClock: NoGrantPastExpiry under ClockPremise, EntryEndsAtExtent, NoStretchUnlessSlow. 535 obligations proved, in discrete time, with no clock rates or margins; checked in 38 rows
A small K_up stops a jammed plane sooner; a large one lets more through under a revoked intent (Consequences)
T_tick and T_intent, small and large (§6's table)

text.tspan: The modules: what each states, what each mutation breaks, and what each abstracts (ADR-0063 §8, ADR-0064 §8)

Under any plane, each honest governor produces fewer than KUp further effects
The two together

A lease a watermark covers produces no further effect (§4's argument)
No lease permits more entries than its count: §4's "at most what is left of its lease's count"

Safe, all four, holds in five rows: KUp = 2 and 3, an honest and a captured plane, and three slots at KUp = 3. Mutations and what each breaks (rows file; the plane is honest unless the row says captured):

Three lease slots, of which Active may be used; a slot is reclaimed once read and released, so leases over a behaviour are unbounded and at most three are outstanding at once. Two governors, honest.
A watermark is one lease's coverage, marked before or after the revocation; a watermark covering several is several delivered together, and the adversary may deliver fewer.
A pushed fence is not modelled: it can only stop a plane or a vehicle earlier, so it subtracts. A plane is not re-seated. An ordered entry is a lease of count one. Reports and ticks do not appear.
A cut link, a late watermark and one never delivered are the same actions, taken or not. Deadlock is not checked: a plane that has stopped is safe.
Checked: 40 rows, all as expected, at KUp = 2, MaxCount = 2, two active slots, unless the row says otherwise (TLC 2.19).
Proved: all 1,871 obligations of Outstanding_proof.tla (f118d16087ce08d2), under the one assumption MaxCount \in Nat (tlapm 7824dab).
Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms: 1,257 closed by tlapm with no backend, 608 by SMT with a proof ethos accepted.
spec/PlaneClock.tla (7d7ced23419c1df2): duration, in explicit discrete time, under §4's premise
No grant under an intent one tick period or more past its expiry, as real time, the expiry being the one the intent named (§4).
A running entry is short of its extent and of the largest extent, in ticks applied, and its governor's own clock has not passed the
next tick's due time (ADR-0062 §4; §5)
A governor whose clock is not slow runs no entry past one overdue tick in real time. Added ⟨R1⟩

ClockPremise: Cardinality(Captured \cup Slow) < Cert, waived only under M_TOOSLOW. Safe holds in seven rows: one captured and one slow of four replicas with a certificate of three (ADR-0061's 4 / 3 / tolerated 2), a fast replica, none faulty, Base =

A grant; a grant after the true expiry, inside the one period of slack
A certificate refuses a grant; refuses a tick
The intent reaches the plane after the tick it names
An entry runs; an entry ends at its extent
A vehicle goes alone; real time passes the next tick's due time
Only with a slow governor: the residual. It holds with a sound or a fast governor (n-stretched-sound, n-stretched-fast)

Discrete time: now in whole units, P units to a period. No clock rates and no margins: a clock is of a class, sound (margin folded in), slow, fast or captured. It says nothing of a real clock's drift.
Going alone is urgent: real time does not pass a running entry's overdue tick by the governor's own clock until the watchdog has acted.

A certificate is one atomic step by at least Cert replicas: no ballot, primary or view (ADR-0061's and Membership.tla's). One intent, one governor, one lease flag, one entry at a time; a lease's ttl is not modelled.
The timing budget is only partly expressible in TLA+ (ToO §11.3), and ADR-0032 defers a timed automaton.
Checked: 38 rows, all as expected (TLC 2.19).
Proved: all 535 obligations of PlaneClock_proof.tla (bbfe21580db67b9d); NoGrantPastExpiryAlways by ClockPremise.
Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms: 334 closed by tlapm with no backend, 195 by SMT with a proof ethos accepted.

A module with explicit time, PlaneClock, states at least NoGrantPastExpiry under a named ASSUME for §4's premise, and EntryEndsAtExtent. Mutations M_ONECLOCK, M_RECEIPT,
M_RELATIVETICK, M_NOWATCHDOG; M_TOOSLOW and NoStretchUnlessSlow added
Met for TLC and TLAPS ⟨R1⟩, in discrete time
The arithmetic of the two rules is transcribed and proved, as mechanism/lean/Topak/Clock.lean does for the subtracting interval
The reference shows a tick refused by a replica whose clock has not reached it, a grant refused while a tick is due, and a lease ended by an overdue tick
Not met: not built
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)

text.tspan: A TTL on a local clock as the safety bound, the first revision

svg.text: Not taken ⟨12⟩. A slow clock preserves authority, which is ADR-0032's test for an interval that needs trusted time
Not taken. ADR-0045 refused one: no issuance fixes a clock's identity
Kept, as the absolute bound. It does not slide, so a long mission needs either a large budget or a new intent for every stretch
Rejected. It fails open under a cut link
Not taken ⟨Q12⟩. The plane's tempo would be that person's attention

Each checker's own clock, with a margin, the first revision

svg.text: Not taken ⟨13⟩. Every clock is then a trust root in the slow direction
Not taken. ADR-0045 refused one

svg.text: Not taken. A timestamp from another party is content (ADR-0032 §3). Here a replica signs or does not, and no time value is exchanged

Not taken ⟨13⟩. An idle plane could act on an intent of any age

text.tspan: Derive duration from the log's order

svg.text: Not available. "Causality orders events and bounds no interval" (ADR-0032)

text.tspan: Consequences, as each record states them

svg.text: The safety bound has no premise about time, and ADR-0032's first clause stands below the intent boundary.
A captured plane is bounded in effects, per honest vehicle, by a check each governor makes itself.
The unread record is bounded by the same number.
The bound is in effects and not in seconds. A plane that idles and then acts on an old intent is inside it. ADR-0064 is
for that.
A jammed plane stops after K_up effects. The trade is declared.
The intent boundary's reading is a trust root for the watermark.
K_up is a placeholder, and nothing here says how to choose it.
One slow clock no longer holds authority open. It takes a certificate's worth of captured and slow replicas.

text.tspan: Every interval has an origin an adversary cannot move.

svg.text: An expiry is a log comparison, the same on every replica and checkable again at apply.
A governor's own clock is a watchdog, and its failure stretches one entry.
A premise about time, which the corpus had kept out of every bound below ADR-0032 §2's second row.
The plane must order one tick per period. A plane that cannot complete a round in T_tick ends its own leases.
Drift accrues from the charter, over the plane's whole life, and the margin has to cover it.
Under a captured plane the duration bound is one clock's again, the honest governor's own.
The floor entry and the reference (§8).
A value for K_up, at least 2 and above any lease's count (§3), and its relation to an intent's budget.
What the intent boundary's checks are, before it orders a watermark.
How a plane comes to know of a captured vehicle (the swarm reading, Z2), which this record does not answer.
The transcription and the reference (§8).
Values for T_tick, T_intent and the margin, as placeholders first, and a measurement of a round.
How far the two rules fit PBFT's validity check (ADR-0061 §2), once PBFT is read.
If the archetype takes it (§7): ADR-0032 a third row, ADR-0031 a ttl in ticks, ADR-0045 the clock's row and finding 2 restated for §5's residual.
